sections.title: Lord of the Flies — Chapter 11 (summary, 2)

paras.text: Jack orders Ralph away from “his end” of the island. Ralph demands Piggy’s glasses back, calling the theft a dirty trick; Jack stabs at him with his spear and the two fight, then break apart. Prompted by Piggy, Ralph pleads for the glasses and for a real signal fire instead of a cooking fire, since a ship may be passing.

paras.text: Piggy, holding up the conch, demands to speak and asks which is better — to have rules and agree, or to hunt and kill; to be sensible like Ralph, or a painted mob. Ralph echoes him: law and rescue, or hunting and breaking things up?

sections.heading: Lord of the Flies — Chapter 11 (summary, 2)
sections.sourceGap: Modern copyrighted novel (William Golding, 1954), printed as a textbook abridgement; paragraph-wise summary in the app, not verbatim. Printed pp. 215–216.

issues.description: The abridgement on p.216 retains, in Piggy’s speech, a racial slur from Golding’s 1954 original; the app summary does not reproduce it. The abridgement also keeps graphic detail of Piggy’s death and Ralph’s profanity (“bloody bloody thief”); summarised without graphic detail. Printed slips noted: “a loud divisive need”, “what amusing thing he might have a say”.
